manifest.name: dsh-builtin-browser
manifest.description: Shared real browser plugin for DeepSeek Harness: install-and-use — a visible native browser the human can take over, driven by the agent over CDP. DOM-level interaction (React/Vue safe), per-task session isolation, cookie persistence (dsh_browser_auth), CAPTCHA detection, batch form fill (dsh_browser_fill), authenticated download, history/replay, action restriction

compatibility._comment: Documentation only. DSH decides plugin compatibility from engines.dsh (falling back to @deepseek-ai/dsh* peerDependencies when it is absent); nothing reads this block. Kept because the release-by-release record is useful to a human and costs nothing.

bundle.text:
# dsh-builtin-browser bundle patch: mounts the shared-browser capability into a
# profile composition.
#
# Row names matter beyond loading: the host's client-module scan resolves a row's
# specifier to a PACKAGE ROOT and reads `dsh.client` from there. A row named after
# a subpath (`dsh-builtin-browser/browser`) is not a package specifier and is
# skipped by design, which would leave the settings panel permanently absent even
# though every tool works — hence the inert root row under the bare package name.
#
# The browser seam (ctx.browser) is always mounted, and the Electron provider plus
# the dsh_browser_* tools are always registered. The CARRIER is chosen at run time:
#
#   1. a browser the user selected in settings (their installed Chrome / Edge),
#      launched with a plugin-owned profile;
#   2. the desktop shell's sidebar, driven over its loopback bridge — the agent
#      then works on the same page the human is looking at;
#   3. a self-hosted Electron window, which is what every surface without either
#      of the above gets; installing the plugin is enough for the browser to work.
#
# DSH 0.2 no longer provides `electronViewHost` (the desktop shell's embedded view),
# so the row below resolves to undefined on current hosts. It keeps reading the
# seam on purpose: a host that reintroduces one is then picked up without a code
# change, and an explicit `viewHost` always outranks the automatic choice.
- insert:
    # Root row. The host's client-module scan resolves a loader row's specifier
    # to a PACKAGE ROOT; a row named after a subpath is skipped, and this package
    # would then have no row to read its `dsh.client` declaration from — the
    # browser would work while its settings panel never appeared. This row is
    # inert (see src/index.ts) and exists only to name the package.
    - id: dsh-builtin-browser
      name: dsh-builtin-browser

    - id: browser
      name: dsh-builtin-browser/browser

    - id: browser-electron
      name: dsh-builtin-browser/browser-electron
      config:
        viewHost: !!js ctx.get('electronViewHost')

    - id: tool-browser
      name: dsh-builtin-browser/tool-browser
      # The tool layer's own switches. The `config` key is what makes them reachable at all:
      # without it nothing at the plugin level could set them, so the operator allow-list the
      # READMEs describe was unreachable in every factory deployment.
      #
      # Every field is optional, so an empty mapping uses the defaults:
      #
      #   allowedActions: operator-level allow-list of browser tool names, applied to every
      #     task in the deployment (a task can still narrow it further with dsh_browser_restrict).
      #     READ_ONLY_TOOLS and dsh_browser_restrict are never blocked, whatever the list says.
      #   timeoutMs: cooperative per-call budget in ms (default 60000).
      #   tabTools: whether the tab-management tools are registered (default true).
      #
      # To restrict a deployment, replace this with, for example:
      #   config:
      #     allowedActions: [dsh_browser_snapshot, dsh_browser_a11y, dsh_browser_content, dsh_browser_click]
      #
      # The settings panel's "What the agent may do" switches are a SEPARATE layer with the
      # same property — the model cannot lift them either — and they need no patch file at
      # all. The list above restricts every task in a deployment; those three switches
      # restrict what any task may do on this installation, and need no YAML.
      config: {}

readme.text: 中文 · English

让 DSH 在内置浏览器、桌面侧栏或本机 Chrome、Edge 中打开网页、读取内容、填写表单和下载文件。每个任务有自己的标签页和操作记录。使用可见窗口或桌面侧栏时，你可以接手 Agent 正在操作的页面。

本页功能清单对应 **0.5.7**（适配 DSH 0.2.2-alpha.3：插件路由走宿主会话鉴权）。[更新记录](CHANGELOG.md)

**先确认你在哪一端** —— 两端是两份独立安装,**更新其中一端不会带上另一端**,浏览器的承载方式也不同。

> **更新已安装的插件是两步**(DSH 0.2.1-alpha.2 起,对已装包再装会直接报 `already-installed`):先 `dsh plugin --profile <profile> remove dsh-builtin-browser`,再 `add` 目标版本。详见[用户指南](docs/user-guide.md#先移除再安装)。

```sh
dsh plugin --profile desktop add dsh-builtin-browser
```

桌面端在外壳支持可驱动的 `<webview>` 且已安装 bridge 时,驱动**官方侧栏**里那个浏览器面板,agent 操作的就是你在界面上看到的同一页面。侧栏不可驱动时自动使用插件自己的 Electron 窗口。

要让插件驱动侧栏,还需要一条 bridge(它装在**桌面端自己的安装目录**里,不在 profile 中)。**0.5.0 起可以一步完成**:

```sh
desktop-bridge/install-and-start.cmd

readme.section: 任意平台:脚本自己关闭 DSH、安装、再启动
readme.text:
node desktop-bridge/install.mjs "<DSH Desktop 安装目录>" --restart
```

`--restart` 由脚本自己关闭桌面端 —— 不要在运行中手工安装:归档被运行中的 Electron 占用,`rename` 会以 `EBUSY` 失败,而"等它退出再装"的守护进程会被一起带走(实测两种拉起方式都如此)。`--restart` 会提示确认,`--yes` 跳过。不带 `--restart` 时脚本仍要求你先关闭桌面端。

> **bridge 是可选项**:不装时自动退回自托管,多出一个独立窗口。**插件或桌面外壳升级后,重跑同一条命令即可修复** —— 桌面端升级会恢复 `app.asar`,桥随之失效,此时 `bridge-status` 报 `stale`。设置在面板顶部可见。载体差异见[已知限制](docs/limitations.md)。

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-builtin-browser
```

Web 端**没有侧栏,也没有 bridge**:共享浏览器由插件**自托管**拉起一个独立窗口(标题 `dsh-browser`),自带完整工具栏(地址栏 / 后退前进刷新 / 标签条),你可以像用普通浏览器一样直接用它。

> 0.5.3 起安装期不下载 Electron、也不带 `postinstall`:运行时要**首次需要时**在后台准备。查看进度和重试都在 **设置 → 浏览器**:准备失败时点「准备内置浏览器」;要在安装阶段提前备好(离线部署 / CI),在该 profile 目录执行 `npx --no dsh-browser-install-electron`(需网络)。详见[用户指南](docs/user-guide.md#准备-electron-二进制)。

完成安装后,直接让 agent 用它:

```
帮我打开 https://example.com，把页面上的主要内容用中文总结一下。
```

浏览器窗口会随第一次调用出现;你可以随时在那个窗口里自己操作,agent 会接着往下走。**两端都可以在设置里改用你本机已安装的 Chrome / Edge**,那是行为完全一致的选项。

| 选项 | 使用方式 |
| --- | --- |
| 内置浏览器 | 在独立窗口中打开页面，提供地址栏、前进、后退、刷新和标签栏。 |
| DSH 侧栏 | 在支持 Electron `webview` 的桌面端安装桥接组件后使用。 |
| 本机 Chrome / Edge | 使用插件专用的浏览器配置启动本机 Chrome 或 Edge。 |
| 自动 | 根据本机浏览器和桌面侧栏的可用情况选择。 |

使用 **DSH 侧栏** 时，在本机 **设置 → 浏览器 → 就绪状态** 点击 **安装桥接**。桌面端升级后可点击 **修复桥接**，已安装时可点击 **重新安装桥接**。安装器自动校验安装目录、安装桥接组件并重启桌面端。也可在插件目录运行：

~~~sh
node desktop-bridge/install.mjs "<DSH Desktop 安装目录>" --restart
~~~

- **就绪状态** 显示浏览器是否可用。展开 **诊断** 查看浏览器选项、内置运行时和桌面桥接状态。
- **安静模式** 保留当前窗口和标签。新启动的 Chrome 和 Edge 在后台运行，最小化的内置浏览器保持最小化。使用桌面侧栏时，先手动打开目标页，再交给 DSH 操作。
- **展示** 提供侧栏自动展开、随会话关闭浏览器、Agent 光标和远程观看开关。
- **Agent 权限** 控制页面脚本、文件下载和登录状态的读写。
- **高级设置** 提供浏览历史、页面定位方式，以及 Chrome 和 Edge 的登录状态保留和窗口模式。交付表单可以设置工具名、参数模板、失败处理和站点规则，校验后一次保存。

在本机或隔离测试环境中打开 **允许远程观看**，通过 DSH 的观看入口查看会话的只读画面。画面以 JPEG 刷新，最高每秒 2 帧。

在 **高级设置 → 交付** 中填入已接入 DSH 的上传工具名，并根据该工具的参数设置目标目录。自动交付使用 DSH 原生工具执行器，保留当前任务的工具权限。文件先保存到本地，再交给所选工具，结果中包含本地路径和上传工具的完整返回值。

例如，百度网盘官方 stdio MCP 的上传工具使用下面的参数模板：

```json
{
  "local_file_path": "{path}",
  "remote_path": "/来自：mcp_server/DSH下载"
}

`{path}` 会替换为已下载文件的完整路径。`remote_path` 是网盘目标文件夹。工具名采用 DSH 中实际注册的名称，格式为 `mcp__<serverName>__upload_file`。[百度网盘 MCP 参数](https://github.com/baidu-netdisk/mcp)

飞书目标可配置具备文件上传能力的 MCP 工具，参数模板按该工具声明的字段填写。

| 用途 | 工具 |
| --- | --- |
| 打开与导航 | `open` `back` `forward` `refresh` `list_tabs` `switch_tab` `close_tab` |
| 读取页面 | `snapshot` `a11y` `content` `scrape` `screenshot` `challenge` |
| 点击与输入 | `click` `click_sequence` `type` `key` `scroll` `drag` `hover` `execute` |
| 填写表单 | `fill` `set_value` `clear` `check` `select` `get_value` |
| 选择与保存文件 | `upload` `download` |
| 执行步骤与核对结果 | `do` `assert` `wait` `wait_for_response` |
| 查看页面状态 | `state` `find` `console` `network` `dialog` |
| 管理会话 | `session` `reset` `reset_session` `restrict` `auth` |
| 查看记录 | `history` `visited` `replay` |
| 排查问题与查用法 | `doctor` `help` |

中文 · English

Use DSH to open pages, read content, fill forms, and download files in the bundled browser, the desktop sidebar, or a local installation of Chrome or Edge. Each task has its own tabs and action history. In a visible window or the desktop sidebar, you can take over the page the agent is using.

This feature list matches **0.5.7** (compatible with DSH 0.2.2-alpha.3: plugin routes go through the host session auth). [Changelog](CHANGELOG.md)

**First, which side are you on** — these are two separate installs; updating one does not update the other, and they host the browser differently.

> **Updating an installed plugin takes two steps** (since DSH 0.2.1-alpha.2, installing over an installed package fails outright with `already-installed`): run `dsh plugin --profile <profile> remove dsh-builtin-browser` first, then `add` the target version. See the [user guide](docs/user-guide.md) (Chinese).

```sh
dsh plugin --profile desktop add dsh-builtin-browser
```

When the desktop shell provides a controllable `<webview>` and the bridge is installed, the plugin drives the **official side panel**: the agent operates the very page you see. Otherwise it falls back to the plugin's own Electron window.

Driving that panel also needs a bridge, installed into **the desktop app's own install directory** rather than the profile:

**Since 0.5.0 this is one step.** The script closes DSH itself — installing while it runs fails with EBUSY on the archive, and a process that waits for the exit is carried away with it:

```sh
desktop-bridge/install-and-start.cmd          # Windows, double-click or run
node desktop-bridge/install.mjs "<dir>" --restart   # any platform
```

> **The bridge is optional**: without it, the plugin uses a standalone window. **Reinstall the bridge with the new script after plugin or desktop shell upgrades** — a desktop update restores `app.asar`, the bridge goes stale, and `bridge-status` reports `stale`. The state is visible at the top of the panel. See [carrier limitations](docs/limitations.md) (Chinese).

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-builtin-browser
```

There is **no side panel and no bridge** on the web side: the shared browser is **self-hosted** in a standalone window (titled `dsh-browser`) with a full toolbar (address bar, back/forward/reload, tab strip) you can use like any browser.

> Since 0.5.3 nothing is downloaded at install time and there is no `postinstall`: the runtime is prepared in the background on first need. Progress and retry live in **Settings → Browser** (use **Prepare the bundled browser** after a failure). To prepare it ahead of time (offline images, CI), run `npx --no dsh-browser-install-electron` from that profile directory (network required). See the [setup guide](docs/user-guide.md#准备-electron-二进制) (Chinese).

Once installation is complete, ask the agent:

```
Open https://example.com and summarise the main content for me.
```

The browser window appears with the first call, and you can operate in it yourself at any point. **Either side can be pointed at your own installed Chrome / Edge** in settings — that option behaves identically on both.

| Option | How it works |
| --- | --- |
| Bundled browser | Opens pages in a separate window with an address bar, navigation controls, and tabs. |
| DSH sidebar | Drives the sidebar on DSH Desktop builds that expose an Electron `webview`, with the bridge installed. |
| Local Chrome / Edge | Launches the installed browser with a dedicated plugin profile. |
| Automatic | Chooses based on the available local browsers and desktop sidebar. |

To use the **DSH sidebar**, click **Install bridge** in the local **Settings → Browser → Readiness** section. Use **Repair bridge** after a desktop update or **Reinstall bridge** when it is already installed. The installer verifies the installation, installs the bridge, and restarts DSH Desktop automatically. You can also run this from the plugin directory:

~~~sh
node desktop-bridge/install.mjs "<DSH Desktop install directory>" --restart
~~~

- **Readiness** reports browser availability. Expand **Diagnostics** to see the browser selection, bundled runtime, and desktop bridge status.
- **Quiet mode** keeps your current window and tab in place. New Chrome and Edge instances run in the background, and minimized bundled browser windows stay minimized. For the desktop sidebar, open the target page by hand before handing it to DSH.
- **Presentation** controls sidebar expansion, closing the browser with the session, the agent cursor, and remote viewing.
- **Agent permissions** controls page scripts, downloads, and reading or writing sign-in state.
- **Advanced settings** covers browsing history, page targeting, and sign-in persistence and window mode for Chrome and Edge. The delivery form validates and saves the tool name, argument template, failure policy, and per-site rules together.

On the local machine or in an isolated test environment, turn on **Allow remote viewing** and open the DSH viewer for a read-only view of the browser session. The viewer refreshes JPEG frames up to twice per second.

In **Advanced settings → Delivery**, enter an upload tool registered in DSH and configure its destination arguments. Automatic delivery uses the DSH native tool executor and retains the current task's tool permissions. The result includes the local download path and the upload tool's complete return value.

The official Baidu Netdisk stdio MCP upload tool accepts this argument template:

```json
{
  "local_file_path": "{path}",
  "remote_path": "/来自：mcp_server/DSH下载"
}

`{path}` becomes the downloaded file's absolute path. `remote_path` names the destination folder. Use the tool name actually registered in DSH, following `mcp__<serverName>__upload_file`. [Baidu Netdisk MCP parameters](https://github.com/baidu-netdisk/mcp)

For Feishu, configure an MCP tool that provides file uploads and use the argument fields it declares.
The current source registers 48 tools. The table lists their names after the `dsh_browser_` prefix.

| Purpose | Tools |
| --- | --- |
| Open and navigate | `open` `back` `forward` `refresh` `list_tabs` `switch_tab` `close_tab` |
| Read pages | `snapshot` `a11y` `content` `scrape` `screenshot` `challenge` |
| Click and type | `click` `click_sequence` `type` `key` `scroll` `drag` `hover` `execute` |
| Fill forms | `fill` `set_value` `clear` `check` `select` `get_value` |
| Select and save files | `upload` `download` |
| Run and verify steps | `do` `assert` `wait` `wait_for_response` |
| Inspect page activity | `state` `find` `console` `network` `dialog` |
| Manage sessions | `session` `reset` `reset_session` `restrict` `auth` |
| Review records | `history` `visited` `replay` |
| Diagnose issues and find help | `doctor` `help` |
